commands.name: git init
commands.description: Initialize a new Git repository in the current directory. This creates a hidden .git folder that tracks all changes.
commands.example:
cd my-project
git init

commands.name: git config
commands.syntax:
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "you@example.com"
commands.description: Set your Git username and email. The --global flag applies it to all repositories on your system.
commands.example:
git config --global user.name "Nayan Jain"
git config --global user.email "nayan@example.com"

commands.name: git version
commands.description: Check which version of Git is installed on your system.
commands.example:
git --version
# Output: git version 2.42.0

commands.name: git clone
commands.description: Create a local copy of a remote repository. Downloads all files, branches, and commit history.
commands.example: git clone https://github.com/username/repo-name.git

commands.name: git remote -v
commands.description: View all remote repositories connected to your local project. Shows fetch and push URLs.
commands.example:
git remote -v
# origin  https://github.com/user/repo.git (fetch)
# origin  https://github.com/user/repo.git (push)

commands.name: git remote add
commands.description: Connect your local repository to a remote repository on GitHub or another hosting service.
commands.example: git remote add origin https://github.com/username/my-project.git

commands.name: git status
commands.description: Show the current state of your working directory. Lists modified, staged, and untracked files.
commands.example:
git status
# On branch main
# Changes not staged for commit:
#   modified: index.html

commands.name: git add
commands.description: Stage files for the next commit. Use '.' to stage all changed files, or specify individual files.
commands.example:
git add index.html      # Stage one file
git add .               # Stage all files

commands.name: git diff
commands.description: Show the exact changes made to files that haven't been staged yet. Shows line-by-line differences.
commands.example:
git diff
git diff --staged    # Show changes that are staged

commands.name: git rm
commands.description: Remove a file from the working directory and stage the deletion for the next commit.
commands.example: git rm old-file.txt

commands.name: git commit
commands.description: Save staged changes as a new commit with a descriptive message. Each commit is a snapshot of your project.
commands.example: git commit -m "Add login page design"

commands.name: git log
commands.description: View the commit history. Use --oneline for a compact view showing commit hash and message.
commands.example:
git log --oneline
# a1b2c3d Add login page
# e4f5g6h Initial commit

commands.name: git show
commands.description: Display detailed information about a specific commit, including the changes made.
commands.example: git show a1b2c3d

commands.name: git commit --amend
commands.description: Modify the most recent commit. Useful for fixing typos in commit messages or adding forgotten files.
commands.example:
git add forgotten-file.js
git commit --amend -m "Add login page with validation"

commands.name: git branch
commands.description: List all branches or create a new branch. The current branch is marked with an asterisk (*).
commands.example:
git branch           # List branches
git branch feature   # Create 'feature' branch

commands.name: git switch
commands.description: Switch to a different branch. This is the modern replacement for 'git checkout' for switching branches.
commands.example:
git switch feature
git switch -c new-feature   # Create and switch

commands.name: git checkout
commands.description: Switch branches or create and switch to a new branch. Older command, still widely used.
commands.example:
git checkout main
git checkout -b bugfix    # Create and switch

commands.name: git branch -d
commands.description: Delete a branch that has been fully merged. Use -D (capital) to force delete an unmerged branch.
commands.example:
git branch -d feature     # Safe delete
git branch -D experiment  # Force delete

commands.name: git merge
commands.description: Combine changes from another branch into the current branch. First switch to the target branch.
commands.example:
git switch main
git merge feature

commands.name: git rebase
commands.description: Reapply your commits on top of another branch. Creates a cleaner, linear history compared to merge.
commands.example:
git switch feature
git rebase main

commands.name: git push
commands.description: Upload your local commits to a remote repository. Shares your work with others.
commands.example:
git push origin main
git push -u origin main   # Set upstream tracking

commands.name: git pull
commands.description: Download and integrate changes from the remote repository. Combines fetch and merge in one step.
commands.example: git pull origin main

commands.name: git fetch
commands.description: Download changes from the remote repository without merging them. Lets you review before integrating.
commands.example:
git fetch origin
git diff main origin/main   # Compare before merging

commands.name: git restore
commands.description: Discard changes in the working directory. Restores a file to its last committed state.
commands.example:
git restore index.html
git restore --staged index.html   # Unstage a file

commands.name: git reset
commands.description: Move the branch pointer to a previous commit. --hard discards all changes (use with caution!).
commands.example:
git reset HEAD~1          # Undo last commit, keep changes
git reset --hard HEAD~1   # ⚠️ Undo last commit, DISCARD changes

commands.name: git stash
commands.description: Temporarily save uncommitted changes and restore a clean working directory. Pop to re-apply them later.
commands.example:
git stash             # Save current changes
git stash pop         # Re-apply saved changes
git stash list        # View all stashes

commands.name: git revert
commands.description: Create a new commit that undoes the changes from a specific commit. Safer than reset for shared branches.
commands.example: git revert a1b2c3d

commands.name: git reflog
commands.description: Show a log of all reference updates. Useful for recovering lost commits or undoing mistakes.
commands.example:
git reflog
# a1b2c3d HEAD@{0}: commit: Add feature
# e4f5g6h HEAD@{1}: checkout: moving from main to feature

commands.name: git clean
commands.description: Remove untracked files and directories. Use -n for a dry run to preview what will be deleted.
commands.example:
git clean -n    # Preview
git clean -fd   # Actually remove

commands.name: git bisect
commands.syntax:
git bisect start
git bisect bad
git bisect good <commit>
commands.description: Use binary search to find the commit that introduced a bug. Very helpful for debugging.
commands.example:
git bisect start
git bisect bad          # Current commit is bad
git bisect good v1.0    # This version was good
